senses.definition: present participle and gerund of slip
The act of something that slips; a slip; a skidding or sudden loosening motion.

quotes.text: Experiments on steep inclines in the United States showed that washing the rails with a detergent to remove oil and grease resulted in a marked improvement; but conditioning the rails with a special neutralising chemical completely eliminated slipping on a bank on which it was so common as to necessitate restriction of trainloads.
quotes.reference: 1956 May, “Eliminating Slipping of Locomotives”, in Railway Magazine, page 280:

quotes.text: The "King" responded well to this treatment and would have maintained 60 m.p.h. up the steepest part had it not been for a brief bout of slipping, which was quickly corrected by Driver Bailes ("Autumn leaves", he remarked laconically).
